## Claims
- [source-backed] \(\Lambda\) has integral Schur basis \(\{s_\lambda\}\), and \(I_{r,q}=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_\lambda:\lambda\nsubseteq q^r\}\) is an ideal with \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\cong H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,r+q})\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- [source-backed] The map \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution of \(\Lambda\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-485]
- [proved] For all \(r,q\ge1\), \(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\); consequently \(\omega\) induces a graded integral ring isomorphism
  \[
  \omega_{r,q}:\Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r},
  \qquad \overline{s_\lambda}\mapsto\overline{s_{\lambda'}},
  \]
  whose inverse is \(\omega_{q,r}\).

## Strategy
Put \(B_{r,q}=\{\lambda:\lambda\subseteq q^r\}\). Then
\[
\lambda\in B_{r,q}
\iff \lambda_1\le q,\ \ell(\lambda)\le r
\iff (\lambda')_1\le r,\ \ell(\lambda')\le q
\iff \lambda'\in B_{q,r}.
\]
Thus conjugation bijects the complementary Schur-basis sets as well. Since \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\),
\[
\omega(I_{r,q})
=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_{\lambda'}:\lambda\notin B_{r,q}\}
=I_{q,r}.
\]

The cited ring-involution property makes \(\omega_{r,q}\) a ring isomorphism. It is integral because it permutes integral Schur bases, and it preserves weight because \(|\lambda'|=|\lambda|\). Since \((\lambda')'=\lambda\), its inverse is precisely \(\omega_{q,r}\).

For \(r=1\), \(B_{1,q}=\{(k):0\le k\le q\}\), mapped to
\(\{(1^k):0\le k\le q\}=B_{q,1}\). For \(q=1\), this is reversed. Hence both boundary cases are included.
